Description: Review code against OWASP Top 10 risks such as Injection, Broken Authentication, Sensitive Data Exposure, and SSRF.
Why: Minimizes vulnerabilities and strengthens the overall security posture.
Comments: Comprehensive security implementation including Helmet.js for HTTP headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options), CSRF protection, input sanitization, SQL injection prevention through parameterized queries, XSS protection, rate limiting, and request validation middleware. Security documentation is present. A formal OWASP audit is recommended.

Description: Ensure credentials, API keys, and tokens are not hardcoded or committed.
Why: Prevents data breaches and unauthorized access.
Comments: Environment variables are used for all secrets and .env files are excluded via .gitignore. Templates are included via .env.example. However, server/.env.backup2 containing real secrets was found committed; this file must be removed and secrets rotated immediately.

Description: Verify endpoints and components enforce role-based permissions.
Why: Prevents privilege escalation and unauthorized actions.
Comments: Casbin RBAC is fully implemented with policy-based access control. Middleware validates all protected endpoints, including admin routes and documentation access. Real-time policy evaluation and group-based permissions provide thorough authorization coverage.

Description: Ensure strong encryption and hashing algorithms are applied where applicable.
Why: Protects confidentiality and aligns with security standards.
Comments: OAuth 2.0 removes the need for password hashing. Session secrets are stored securely via environment variables. HTTPS is enforced in production. No evidence of encryption at rest was found. No bcrypt or Argon2 usage is present, though possibly unnecessary for OAuth-based auth. Session cookies use HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

Description: Verify that PII is handled according to GDPR, HIPAA, or similar regulations.
Why: Reduces legal and reputational risks.
Comments: User data handling and audit logging exist. Missing GDPR/HIPAA-specific measures, data retention policies, and user data deletion/export capabilities. PII handling should be reviewed for regulatory compliance.

Description: Validate API inputs and server-side payloads.
Why: Prevents malicious input and ensures data integrity.
Comments: Zod schemas, sanitization middleware, validation middleware, XSS and SQL injection checks, and parameterized queries are implemented. Type validation exists throughout. Backend validation is robust.

Description: Ensure consistent and structured handling of runtime errors.
Why: Prevents crashes, improves reliability, and maintains predictable error output.
Comments: Centralized error handler, standardized error response formats, structured logging, production-safe output without stack traces, request ID correlation, and mapped error types. Error handling is well implemented.

Description: Automate build, test, and deployment processes.
Why: Ensures reliable delivery and reduces manual deployment risk.
Comments: Test infrastructure exists for Jest, Vitest, and Playwright. However, no CI/CD pipeline is present, no GitHub Actions workflows exist, and deployments are manual. Tasks.md lists CI/CD Pipeline at 0%.

Description: Integrate metrics, dashboards, and alerts.
Why: Allows proactive detection of failures and performance issues.
Comments: Prometheus metrics, structured logging, request ID tracking, and Grafana dashboards exist. Alerting rules are missing and production deployment steps are incomplete.

Description: Document procedures for reverting deployments.
Why: Minimizes downtime and deployment risks.
Comments: A basic rollback approach is noted but lacks detail, testing, and database rollback processes. A formal rollback strategy is required.

Description: Define a peer review process for major code changes.
Why: Improves quality and encourages shared ownership.
Comments: A detailed code review checklist exists, but there is no automated PR review flow, no branch protection rules, and no mandatory review enforcement.

Description: Test individual functions and components.
Why: Ensures correctness and supports refactoring.
Comments: Unit tests exist for various utilities and modules using Jest and Vitest. Test coverage reporting is available; coverage percentage has not been verified.

Description: Maintain consistent log entries for significant events and errors.
Why: Improves debugging, monitoring, and incident investigation.
Comments: Structured logging, correlation IDs, contextual logging, log levels, and audit trails are implemented comprehensively.

Description: Optimize SQL queries and database indexes.
Why: Prevents performance bottlenecks and reduces load.
Comments: Indexes exist for key fields, parameterized queries are used, optimization docs exist, and index hints are used. Query performance monitoring could be expanded.

Description: Provide detailed architecture and system design documentation.
Why: Ensures shared understanding and consistent design decisions.
Comments: Architecture, component documentation, API design, and system overview exist, supported by a VitePress documentation site.

Description: Provide API specifications using Swagger/OpenAPI.
Why: Enables easy integration and testing by internal and external teams.
Comments: Swagger UI and OpenAPI spec are fully implemented with examples, schemas, and security definitions.

Description: Test interactions between modules and services.
Why: Detects communication or coordination issues between components.
Comments: Integration tests exist using Supertest and mocks. Coverage likely varies.

Description: Automate user workflow testing.
Why: Ensures system correctness under realistic usage.
Comments: Playwright is configured with multiple E2E tests. Coverage may be limited and could be expanded.

Description: Measure code coverage for all automated tests.
Why: Improves reliability and prevents regressions.
Comments: Coverage reporting exists for Jest and Vitest. Actual coverage percentage is unknown. A >70% target is referenced but unverified.

Description: Measure response time, resource usage, and throughput.
Why: Ensures performance and scalability targets are met.
Comments: Prometheus metrics and optimization documentation exist. No formal benchmarks or load testing results are documented.

Description: Verify constraints, relationships, and data consistency.
Why: Prevents invalid data states and reduces complexity.
Comments: Database constraints, foreign keys, and type validation exist. Further constraint validation may be beneficial.

Description: Use environment variables for all environments.
Why: Improves security, portability, and deployment consistency.
Comments: Environment variables are used throughout with templates and separated config files. A committed backup .env file must be removed.

Description: Maintain versioned migration scripts.
Why: Ensures consistent schema evolution and safe deployments.
Comments: Schema SQL files exist but no formal migration system is used. Versioned migrations and automation should be implemented.

Description: Document the development setup process.
Why: Reduces onboarding time and ensures consistency.
Comments: Comprehensive documentation, setup scripts, and prerequisites exist.

Description: Provide the main project overview and instructions.
Why: Gives developers a quick entry point into the project.
Comments: Rich documentation including setup, features, scripts, and architecture links. Well organized.

Description: Implement client-side validation.
Why: Improves UX and prevents common input errors early.
Comments: Vue validation exists but could be more comprehensive. Some logic relies on backend validation.

Description: Use consistent and descriptive IDs for UI elements.
Why: Improves test automation and maintainability.
Comments: Some components lack consistent IDs and no naming convention exists. Enhancements would support reliable E2E testing.

Description: Apply a unified design language.
Why: Ensures visual consistency and reduces design debt.
Comments: Vuetify is used consistently with theme support, color configuration, and RTL support. Additional UI/UX improvements are planned.

Description: Ensure UI adapts across screen sizes.
Why: Improves usability on all devices.
Comments: Vuetify responsive grid, mobile navigation, and responsive design tests exist. Responsiveness is well implemented.

Description: Include standardized headers for all files.
Why: Improves traceability and organizational clarity.
Comments: File headers with metadata and JSDoc are consistently applied.

Description: Document parameters, returns, and behavior.
Why: Prevents misuse and improves maintainability.
Comments: Extensive JSDoc coverage with parameter definitions, return types, examples, and error annotations.

Description: Use static analysis to enforce code standards.
Why: Prevents style drift and reduces defects.
Comments: ESLint and Prettier are configured with lint scripts. Enforcement in CI/CD is missing due to absent pipeline.

Description: Maintain consistent naming patterns.
Why: Improves readability and onboarding.
Comments: Consistent naming conventions across files, variables, functions, and classes.

Description: Use semantic versioning with optional automation.
Why: Communicates change impact and release stability.
Comments: Semantic versioning is used but lacks automated incrementing.

Description: Provide summaries of new features and fixes.
Why: Keeps stakeholders informed.
Comments: A changelog exists, but release note completeness varies. No formal process is defined.

Description: Create consistent branch naming standards.
Why: Improves collaboration and CI automation.
Comments: No documented branch naming convention or workflow exists.

Description: Support multiple locales and languages.
Why: Enables global usability.
Comments: Vue i18n implemented with English and Arabic support, including RTL support. Strong localization support.

Description: Use AI tools to improve productivity.
Why: Improves speed and consistency in development.
Comments: Limited documentation of AI usage; not formally integrated into workflow.

Description: Add comments explaining complex logic.
Why: Helps maintainers understand non-obvious logic.
Comments: Good use of inline comments explaining rationale and intent.

Description: Generate documentation from structured comments.
Why: Keeps technical documentation current.
Comments: JSDoc is used extensively with HTML generation. Doxygen is not implemented.

Description: Limit maximum line length for readability.
Why: Improves cross-editor readability.
Comments: Prettier likely enforces reasonable limits, but no explicit policy exists.

Description: Use clear and consistent commit messages.
Why: Improves traceability and debugging.
Comments: No commit message convention or validation exists. Quality varies.
